metadata.title: Data pipeline
metadata.description: Where the site's data comes from, and how it is harvested and stored.

intro.title: Data pipeline
intro.lead: This page documents where the site's data comes from. It covers the external sources, the harvest jobs that fetch data from them, the order the jobs run in, and how the database stores the result. The text describes the working code, and the database section is generated from the live database, so the two cannot drift apart. The page shows no row counts, because counts change every time a job runs. To see current counts and harvest times, call GET /api/v1/'{'code'}'/meta/freshness.

sources.heading: External sources
sources.lead: The database receives data from fourteen inputs. Eleven of them are services on the network. One is a set of CSV files kept in this repository. One is a read-only connection to the previous platform's Postgres database. One is a language model that runs locally. The Used by column names the harvest steps that read each source, and a step marked manual runs only when someone starts it by hand.
sources.openalexProvides: The journal universe, works, author profiles, publishers, funders, and open-access color samples.
sources.openalexTransport: REST API. The list comes in pages, and each response includes the cursor for the next page. Single-work requests are preferred over batch filters. Uses OPENALEX_API_KEY when set.
sources.openalexUsedBy: Bootstrap steps journals, publishers, oa-colors, stats, enrich, and author-ids. Manual steps funder sweeps, work funders, and the Emerald contract import.
sources.crossrefProvides: DOI metadata used to resolve journals.
sources.crossrefTransport: REST API through the stavrophora client, 50 DOIs per request, capped at 3 requests per second, in the polite pool. A malformed DOI that fails the batch is isolated by splitting the batch until the bad DOI stands alone.
sources.openaireProvides: The institution's research products and a curated funder canon.
sources.openaireTransport: REST API through the aireloom client, 100 per page. Skips the institution when no org id is configured.
sources.openaireUsedBy: Bootstrap step openaire. Manual step funder canon.
sources.pureOaiProvides: The institution's publications, CERIF author lists, org units, and persons.
sources.pureOaiTransport: OAI-PMH ListRecords with resumption tokens. At least 1 second between requests. Anonymous access.
sources.pureOaiUsedBy: Bootstrap steps pure, pure-cerif, and pure-entities.
sources.openaccessNlTransport: HTML pages scraped strictly one at a time.
sources.jctProvides: Deal ESAC ids and journal lists.
sources.jctTransport: Published Google Sheets as CSV, with a 0.5 to 1.5 second pause between agreements.
sources.openapcProvides: Per-article APC and transformative agreement costs.
sources.openapcTransport: Five CSV files from the project's GitHub raw storage.
sources.doajProvides: The open-access journal canon with APC flags.
sources.doajTransport: One full CSV download from doaj.org/csv.
sources.scimagoProvides: SJR indicator and quartile per year.
sources.scimagoTransport: Seed CSVs tracked in the repository at backend/data/scimagojr. The Scimago site blocks scripted downloads.
sources.jiscProvides: Publisher OA policies, the funder canon, and a repository list.
sources.jiscTransport: REST API with an x-api-key header and search_after paging, 0.15 seconds between requests by default.
sources.ipApiTransport: Batch POST of up to 100 IPs, 4.5 seconds between calls on the free tier.
sources.purePortalProvides: Organisation parents and person-org links the OAI feed lacks.
sources.purePortalTransport: RSS pages fetched with a browser user agent, 2 seconds between requests.
sources.utMetadataProvides: Canonical works of the previous platform.
sources.utMetadataTransport: A read-only Postgres connection through JB_UT_METADATA_DSN. No HTTP requests.
sources.utMetadataUsedBy: Bootstrap step authors with --source utmd, one-time importers, and development checks.
sources.embeddingsTransport: The model runs locally through fastembed and ONNX. No network requests.

calls.openalexJournalsRequest: GET /sources, 100 records per page. Each response includes the cursor for the next page. A batched request seeds the deal journals. The institution is found by searching for its ROR id.
calls.openalexPublishersRequest: GET /publishers in batches of 50 ids. A second request on demand fetches the top of the ownership chain.
calls.openalexOaColorsRequest: GET /works per journal, filtered to the primary location source, 20 newest works, 4 journals in parallel.
calls.openalexStatsRequest: GET /works with cursor paging, filtered to the institution id and the data window. One count request per year counts works with a corresponding author from the institution.
calls.openalexEnrichRequest: GET /works/'{'doi'}', one request per DOI, in chunks of 500 with 10 requests in flight.
calls.openalexAuthorIdsRequest: GET /authors with cursor paging, filtered by the institution's ROR, 200 per page. Then GET /works for 50 author ids per request.
calls.crossrefEnrichRequest: GET /works with a doi filter listing 50 DOIs per request, sent through the polite pool.
calls.pureWorksRequest: OAI ListRecords in the oai_dc metadata format, one OAI set per publication year in the data window.
calls.pureWorksWrites: source_records, works (upsert, retire on full sweep)
calls.pureCerifRequest: OAI ListRecords in the oai_cerif_openaire format, set openaire_cris_publications.
calls.pureEntitiesRequest: OAI ListRecords in the same format, sets openaire_cris_orgunits and openaire_cris_persons.
calls.openaireRequest: GET /researchProducts through the aireloom client, 100 per page, filtered to the institution's org id.
calls.dealsOpenaccessRequest: GET the overview page, then each publisher page, then each deal page, one request at a time.
calls.dealsJctRequest: GET the index sheet as CSV, then one CSV per agreement, pausing 0.5 to 1.5 seconds between downloads.
calls.dealsReconcileRequest: No network. Merges rows on ESAC id, enforces unique agreement data, writes a curation report to landing/reports.
calls.dealsIssnLRequest: No network. Fills missing coverage ISSNs from issn_map.
calls.doajRequest: GET the full CSV from https://doaj.org/csv.
calls.scimagoRequest: No network. Unpacks the seed CSVs kept in the repository.

dag.heading: Harvest order
dag.planLead: Bootstrap is the script at backend/jobs/bootstrap.py. It plans the work in three groups, and this page calls the groups bands. The global band runs once for the whole deployment. The institution band runs once for every hosted institution. The final band holds one step, journal embeddings. Bootstrap starts each step as a separate process the moment that step's dependencies have finished, so independent branches run at the same time. When a step fails, bootstrap starts no new steps, lets the running steps finish, and exits with an error code. The deployment then refuses to start the backend, because the database is only partly filled.
dag.clientLead: Every HTTP call in the harvest jobs uses the same client settings. A request times out after 120 seconds. When an API answers with 429 or a temporary server error, the client retries the request up to three times. It waits as long as the Retry-After header asks when the API sends one, and otherwise it waits longer after each attempt, up to 60 seconds.
dag.modesLead: Bootstrap has three run modes, and auto mode is the default. Auto mode skips the whole plan when two things are true. The journals table has rows, and the plan wrote its completion marker. The marker is one harvest_state row with source local and entity bootstrap_plan, and the plan runner writes it after the plan finishes without error. Journals without the marker mean an earlier bootstrap stopped partway. In that case auto mode refuses to run and exits with error 1 instead of skipping. Repair mode, started with --from STEP, reruns the plan from one step onward, one step at a time. --institution CODE runs the plan for a single institution, which is how a new institution joins an existing deployment.
dag.perCodeCaption: The institution band runs once per hosted code. Dependencies that cross bands read from the global band.
dag.generatedCaption: The step list, scripts, and dependencies come from jobs/bootstrap.py. backend/scripts/dump_harvest_plan.py generated them on {date}. The diagram checks its arrows against the same file when the site builds, so the picture and the list cannot disagree.

jobs.heading: How each source is harvested
jobs.openalexIntro: The journals job retrieves the full OpenAlex sources list, 100 records per page. Each response includes the cursor value for the next page. The job sends that value back on every following request, until the API reports the end of the list. The job writes one row per journal into journals, keyed by ISSN-L. ISSN-L is the standard id that groups a journal's print, online, and variant ISSNs under one id, and the job maps every variant ISSN to it in issn_map. With --seed-deals-only, the same job does less. It writes only the journals covered by a deal, in batches of 50. The publishers job runs after it and resolves each journal's publisher lineage from OpenAlex publisher ids, 50 at a time. It makes a second pass for lineage roots, the publishers at the top of an ownership chain.
jobs.openalexInstitutionJobs: Five institution-side jobs read OpenAlex. The stats job sweeps every work of the institution, 100 per page, and counts per year how many works had an institution author as the corresponding author. The enrich job asks OpenAlex about each work DOI, one DOI per request, in chunks of 500 with 10 requests in flight. That stays far below OpenAlex's published limit of 100 requests per second, and each single-work request costs 1 credit of the 100,000 credits a free key gets per day. When OpenAlex has no work for a DOI, the job records the identity as missing, so the Crossref pass only covers DOIs worth trying. The author-ids job sweeps authors affiliated with the institution's ROR id, 200 per page, and then fetches the works of the authors it resolved, 50 author ids per request, up to 2000 authors per run. The OA color job samples the 20 newest works of each open-access journal, four journals at a time. It fills only colors it has not observed yet, so an interrupted run can continue.
jobs.crossrefIntro: Crossref is the second identity source. The enrich job sends the DOIs that OpenAlex could not resolve in batches of 50. The contact email in each request tells Crossref who is asking, which puts the client in Crossref's polite pool, the pool with steadier response times. A confirmed match writes the same work_identity rows as OpenAlex and resolves the journal through issn_map. The third rung needs no network at all. Works that still have no journal are checked against the CERIF ISSN recorded on the work itself.
jobs.pureProtocol: Three passes read the same Pure OAI-PMH endpoint at ris.utwente.nl. OAI-PMH is a standard XML protocol for harvesting repository content. The passes are anonymous, wait at least one second between requests, and read each set page by page. Each response includes a resumption token, the id that requests the next page. If a token goes stale, the pass restarts that set, at most twice.
jobs.purePasses: The works pass requests one OAI set per publication year in the data window, in a simple metadata format. A full sweep also retires works that have disappeared from Pure by stamping their retired_at time. The CERIF pass requests the CERIF publication set, which uses a richer metadata format. From it, the pass fills each work's CERIF ISSN, publisher, DOI, and open-access status, plus the work-to-author edges in work_pure_authors. The entities pass requests the org unit and person sets, and rebuilds pure_orgs, pure_org_parents, and pure_persons from the stored records.
jobs.openaireIntro: The openaire job runs when the institution has an openaire_org_id. It retrieves the OpenAIRE Graph API's research products, 100 per page, which is the API's maximum, and stores every payload verbatim. When a product's DOI matches a local work, the job confirms that work's identity. When only the title matches, the job records a candidate row for a person to review, instead of claiming a match.
jobs.dealsHarvests: Two independent harvests feed one merged deal register. The openaccess.nl scraper reads the deal overview page, then each publisher page, then each deal page. It sends one request at a time, and it stores every HTML page before parsing it. The JCT job reads the published index sheet, and then one CSV per agreement. It waits a random 0.5 to 1.5 seconds between downloads, because Google throttles rapid fetching.
jobs.dealsMerge: The reconcile job merges the two sources. It pairs an openaccess.nl row with a JCT row when the publisher names match ignoring case and the deal durations overlap, and it treats rows with the same ESAC id as the same agreement. The merge compares one field, the deal status. When the two sources disagree on status, the row gets needs_curation set, with both values in the reason. The other JCT fields, the ESAC id, the data URL, the corresponding-authors-only flag, and the last-reviewed date, are copied over as they are. Rows for foreign consortium partners never merge. Deals an admin removed stay excluded, and manual_overrides are reapplied after every run. A final pass resolves each deal journal's coverage ISSN to its ISSN-L through issn_map and flags the rows it cannot resolve.
jobs.openapcDoajScimagoIntro: The OpenAPC job downloads five CSV files from the project's GitHub raw storage, keeps landing copies, and rebuilds two tables by replacing their contents. The tables are journal_apc_aggregates, one row per ISSN-L and period, and apc_evidence for the home institution. The job then refreshes journals.latest_apc_euro. The DOAJ job downloads the site's full journal CSV once and stamps journals with is_in_doaj, the DOAJ APC facts, and the DOAJ homepage, matching by ISSN. An open-access journal that DOAJ does not list gets is_in_doaj set to false explicitly. The Scimago job unpacks the seed CSVs kept in the repository, because the Scimago site blocks scripted downloads. It writes scimagojr_metrics rows per ISSN-L and year, and stamps journals.in_scimago and latest_quartile.
jobs.identityWorkIntro: Work identity follows simple rules. An exact DOI match confirms the row immediately, with matched_by doi and confidence 1.0. Title matching against OpenAIRE scores trigram similarity, needs at least 0.82, keeps only the best-scoring work per record, and always writes the row as candidate for a person to review. It never writes confirmed. A 404 from Crossref or OpenAlex writes missing, which means nothing was found, not that confidence was low. The only other way a row becomes confirmed is an admin flipping it in review, and harvest writes never overwrite that decision. The vocabulary also allows matched_by verbatim, a match on the shared source string. No harvest flow writes it today; the value is reserved.
jobs.identityAuthorIntro: Author identity checks five rungs in order, and each rung writes its own fixed confidence. An exact ORCID match scores 1.0. Equal normalized full names score 0.9. Matching initials forms score 0.8. A family name that is unique among the work's Pure authors scores 0.7. Fuzzy name similarity of at least 0.92 by Levenshtein ratio scores 0.6. Each rung must produce exactly one unambiguous match. If a rung is ambiguous, the next rung is used instead. Admins flip author identity rows in review, with the same three statuses: confirmed, candidate, and rejected. A rejected match is sticky. Later runs never re-propose the same id, and the resolver never lowers an admin's confirmed or rejected decision. Every flip writes an audit row to status_changes.

scheduling.heading: Scheduling
scheduling.lead: Nothing runs on a schedule. The only automatic invocation is the compose bootstrap service. Every docker compose up runs the alembic migrations and bootstrap.py before the backend starts, and auto mode exits in seconds once the plan-completion marker shows a completed run, so restarts are cheap. JB_BOOTSTRAP=always forces a full rerun, and repair mode reruns from one step. Any other fresh data arrives only when someone starts a job by hand. The manual table below is never run automatically.
scheduling.loopsLead: Two serving-side loops run continuously, and neither harvests anything. A nightly job nulls usage-event IP addresses older than 90 days, and an in-process loop refreshes deal coverage flags. For live freshness, GET /api/v1/'{'code'}'/meta/freshness reports each source's harvest state, which is the source, entity type, filter set, status, last finished time, and stats. It also reports the newest row timestamps for the main serving tables, and the degraded list. The degraded list names serving-time helpers that currently answer without their normal backing data. The deal-flag refresh loop marks itself degraded when its background refresh fails, and the currency-rate helper marks itself degraded when the rate table fails to load or a conversion finds no rate. The limitations table is a different registry. It is a curated list of known data caveats, seeded by migration, served at GET /api/v1/'{'code'}'/meta/limitations, and cited by code in journal API responses.
scheduling.runbookLead: The runbook below maps every bootstrap step to its script. The steps, scripts, and dependencies come from the generated plan, and institution-band steps run with --institution CODE.

manual.heading: What bootstrap does not fetch
manual.lead: These jobs live in the repository, and the bootstrap plan never calls them. Some repair one bad run. Some backfill data the pipeline does not cover. Some are development checks. A fresh deployment works without them until someone runs them by hand.
manual.harvestJiscWhat: Sweeps the Jisc Open Policy Finder with an API key and normalizes the result into the canon tables. Stamps the journals.jisc_* policy columns.
manual.harvestJiscWrites: jisc_publications, jisc_publishers, jisc_policies, jisc_funders, jisc_funder_groups, jisc_repositories, journals.jisc_*
manual.harvestOpenAlexFundersWhat: Sweeps all OpenAlex funders, 200 per page.
manual.harvestOpenaireFundersWhat: Writes a curated OpenAIRE funder canon (NWO, EC, Wellcome, NSF) and its top-level funding streams.
manual.harvestWorkFundersWhat: Fetches funder and grant rows for every work that has a DOI, one request per work in chunks of 500.
manual.importPureExportWhat: Imports a Pure backend OAI export file as full CERIF records.
manual.harvestPurePortalWhat: Fills missing pure_org_parents from the public portal RSS, 2 seconds between requests.
manual.harvestPortalPersonsWhat: Binds portal person listings to persons and orgs.
manual.importUtmetadataRawWhat: One-time copy of ut-metadata raw works into the local landing store, then rebuilds the stats.
manual.importUtmetadataWorksWhat: One-time copy of ut-metadata canonical works into works.
manual.ingestEmeraldContractWhat: Rebuilds one deal's journal list from the signed contract spreadsheet.
manual.enrichUsageGeoWhat: Backfills usage_events.country from ip-api.com in batches of up to 100 IPs.
manual.verifyUtmetadataWhat: Development check that the local corpus matches ut-metadata. Writes a report, no data.
manual.funderLinkMatrixWhat: Reports how many Jisc funders have OpenAlex and OpenAIRE twins. Writes to stdout only.

config.heading: Configuration
config.lead: All configuration lives in environment variables that start with JB_. The first institutions row is also seeded from them. Migration 0019 inserts the default row when the database upgrades, and ensure_home_institution re-derives the same fields on the first harvest by matching on the ROR id. It fills the code, which is the lowercased JB_INSTITUTION_CODE, plus the names, the Pure OAI URL, the OpenAIRE org id, and the data window. To onboard another institution, create one institutions row and run bootstrap --institution CODE.
config.purposeDatabaseUrl: The main Postgres connection string, using the asyncpg driver.
config.purposeUtMetadataDsn: Read-only connection to the previous platform's Postgres. Without it, the authors job skips its ut-metadata source.
config.purposeOpenAlexApiKey: OpenAlex API key. Without a key, runs share the smaller keyless budget.
config.purposeContactEmail: Contact email sent with requests, so Crossref and OpenAlex can identify the client.
config.purposeJiscApiKey: API key for the Jisc Open Policy Finder, used by the manual Jisc jobs.
config.purposeDataWindow: The publication-year window the harvest covers. The start defaults to 2020, and an empty end means open ended. The window sets the Pure OAI year sets and the OpenAlex date filters.
config.purposeInstitutionIdentity: The hosted institution's identity. The code may contain lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens.
config.purposeOpenaireOrgId: The institution's OpenAIRE organization id. It cannot be derived from the ROR id, and every institution other than the default needs one.
config.purposePureOaiUrl: The Pure OAI-PMH endpoint. Requests are anonymous.
config.purposeLandingDir: Where downloaded files are kept permanently. The default is landing/.
config.purposeAdminPassword: The admin panel password. An empty value disables the panel.

storage.heading: How data is stored
storage.leadRaw: Every harvested payload is stored twice, first as raw bytes and then as a parsed record. The download helper writes the bytes under landing/ and adds a raw_files row. An ingest session then stores the parsed payload in source_records, and each record stores a SHA-256 hash of its content plus the source, entity type, and source key. When a re-harvest produces identical content, the job inserts nothing. When the content changed, the job adds a new version. Old versions are never deleted, so this history grows without limit. The normalized tables, such as journals, works, openalex_works, deals, the Pure tables, and the Jisc tables, are rebuilt from these stored copies. Because the copies are kept, every job can run again and reach the same result.
storage.leadDerived: A third layer precomputes the values the site reads on every page. journal_flags holds one row per journal per hosted institution. The layer also fills works_2020_plus, latest_apc_euro, publisher_canonical, oa_status_observed, the stored search_vector column, and the embedding vectors. Every run is recorded in harvest_runs and harvest_state, and every finished run, completed or failed, bumps cache_epoch, the single-row table that keys the site's in-process caches. A run bumps the epoch even when it fails, because a run commits its data page by page, and those pages can change what the site serves before the run closes. The facet and snapshot caches live for 24 hours and check this epoch on every read. The refresh jobs for the precomputed values bump the epoch directly as well.
storage.leadSiteWrites: The site writes some tables itself, without any harvest. usage_events holds batched page views, searches, and errors. A nightly job nulls the raw IP addresses after 90 days, and it keeps the rows and their country codes. feedback_items keeps the reporter's search state. doc_edits are admin edits applied over the served documents. manual_overrides are admin corrections that are reapplied after every harvest. author_identities and work_identity hold review decisions. status_changes is an append-only audit log.

storage.stageSourceRecordsDetail: Verbatim payloads, versioned by content hash.
storage.stageNormalizedDetail: journals, works, openalex_works, deals, pure_*, jisc_*, authors
storage.stageDenormalizedDetail: journal_flags, works_2020_plus, latest_apc_euro, publisher_canonical, oa_status_observed, search_vector, embedding
storage.stageDocEditsDetail: Admin edits applied over the served documents.

serving.heading: How the site serves this data
serving.searchLead: Journal search runs every listing through one shared query, base_query in services/search/query.py. The query joins each journal to the institution's journal_flags row. It keeps journal-type venues with more than 3 works in the data window, and it keeps every other venue type with at least one institution work. Journals marked browse_excluded are never served. Relevance ranking uses three signals, in this order. A match on the title prefix ranks highest, the Postgres full-text rank comes next, and a small works count bonus breaks ties. Facets run over the same filtered set of journals and are cached for 24 hours, keyed on the cache epoch. The journal detail page assembles the journal row, its deal coverage, its per-year institution stats from both the Pure canon and OpenAlex, Scimago quartiles, APC aggregates and evidence, the raw venue record, and the works stored in openalex_works.
serving.oaTypeLead: The journal's oa_type is computed at query time and never stored. The rules below apply in order, and the first match wins.
serving.oaStatusLead: A missing flag is not treated as false. A NULL doaj_in_doaj means the DOAJ sweep never judged that journal. Work-level oa_status works differently. The harvest stores it, and the stored value comes from a fixed six-value vocabulary. The funder fit tiers build on oa_type and the Jisc green-route columns, which say whether a submitted, accepted, or published version may be posted, and after how many embargo months. One SQL expression computes the tiers, and the same expression is mirrored in Python.
serving.embeddingsLead: Journals are embedded as 384-dimension vectors built from the cleaned title, the top five topics, and the titles of up to three of the journal's most-cited works. The model is BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5, running locally on CPU through fastembed and ONNX. A pgvector HNSW index serves similar-journal lists in three scopes, the institution, the deals, and everything, and it also serves semantic search. Author recommendations average the vectors of an author's venues, weighted by work counts. The embeddings step runs once, after every institution's stats step, and it is the last bootstrap step.
serving.apiContractLead: The API contract is generated, not hand-written. openapi.json at the repository root is dumped from the routes, CI fails when it drifts, and the frontend's lib/api-types.ts is generated from it.
